data.title: Privacy coins face diverging fortunes as KuCoin moves to drop Monero
data.description:
Crypto exchange KuCoin said Thursday it will delist Monero on Nov. 30, making it the second major platform this month to drop the privacy coin. Exchange MEXC suspended XMR spot trading and delisted its perpetual futures contracts earlier in November.

KuCoin has already suspended XMR deposits and plans to close withdrawals on Dec. 31. XMR fell 10.5% to $449.98 as of 7:00 p.m. UTC on Thursday. The drop extends a decline from about $625 on Nov. 3.

The delisting comes as the European Union prepares to restrict privacy coins on regulated platforms. Starting July 10, 2027, the bloc’s Anti-Money Laundering Regulation will prohibit financial firms, including crypto asset service providers, from maintaining anonymous accounts or accounts that obscure transactions through “anonymity-enhancing coins,” regardless of whether the privacy features are enabled by default or optional. The regulation does not prohibit individuals from holding privacy coins in self-custody wallets.

Launched in 2014, Monero conceals transaction amounts and the wallet addresses of senders and recipients by default. Unlike Monero, Zcash (ZEC), launched in 2016, allows users to choose between transparent and shielded transactions. Both cryptocurrencies have faced regulatory scrutiny over the past few years, with Binance delisting Monero in 2024 and Kraken ending support for it in the European Economic Area later that year.

Zach Pandl, head of research at Grayscale, which launched the first US spot ZEC exchange-traded fund (ETF) in August, said Zcash is positioned differently from Monero. He told Cointelegraph that the firm’s commitment to Zcash will continue for “many years to come.”

Delistings mount ahead of EU privacy coin restrictions

KuCoin’s delisting of Monero follows a series of similar moves by crypto exchanges amid growing regulatory pressure on privacy coins. Since 2018, when Japan’s Financial Services Agency pressed exchanges to drop anonymity coins, regulators in other jurisdictions, including South Korea and Dubai, have also taken steps to restrict their use or availability.

In Europe, plans to restrict privacy coins emerged as early as 2022, when a leaked draft of an Anti-Money Laundering bill came to light. The EU’s regulation defines “anonymity-enhancing coins” as cryptocurrencies with built-in features that anonymize transaction data “either systematically or optionally,” which could bring cryptocurrencies with opt-in privacy features, such as Zcash, within the scope of the restrictions.

Pandl said that viewing keys allow Zcash holders to disclose transactions “to an auditor or regulator, law enforcement if they need.” He said the feature gives users greater control over who can access their financial information. “That is exactly how the financial system works today. It’s just that it gives the authority to individuals rather than institutions,” he said.

However, whether viewing keys alone can satisfy regulatory requirements remains a point of debate.

Other approaches to privacy are gaining traction among traditional financial institutions looking to use public blockchains. In April, Paris-based digital asset infrastructure provider Dfns partnered with cryptography firm Zama to bring confidential transactions to its more than 400 enterprise clients, including banks, fintechs and custodians. The collaboration uses encryption to conceal transaction amounts and balances on public blockchains while allowing authorized parties to access the information for compliance purposes.

Grayscale says shielding beats obfuscation

Grayscale has offered exposure to ZEC since the launch of its Zcash Trust in 2017, based on the view that transaction privacy would be essential for financial institutions to adopt public blockchains.

Pandl said that as AI has advanced, it has become “much easier to link pseudonymous addresses with offchain information.” Monero, he explained, uses ring signatures that obscure the source of transactions among multiple possible signers, a method Pandl said “may be vulnerable” as AI-powered blockchain analytics improve.

“We believe strongly that Zcash is the stronger tech,” he said, because “it takes a shielding approach rather than an obfuscation approach.” Zcash uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify shielded transactions without publicly revealing sensitive transaction data onchain.

Monero developers, however, are working on an upgrade that would replace ring signatures with a zero-knowledge proof system in a bid to enhance transaction privacy.

“For public blockchain technology to become a mainstream part of the financial system, it absolutely needs a privacy layer,” Pandl said.

ETF conviction despite outflows

Grayscale’s Zcash ETF began trading on NYSE Arca on Aug. 25, following the conversion of its Zcash Trust. While investors seeking to use Zcash’s privacy features would need to hold the cryptocurrency directly, “the ETF can provide the store of value use case of these [privacy] technologies,” Pandl said.

Grayscale’s ETF reached $1 billion in assets under management on Sept. 24, but that figure had fallen to $406 million on Wednesday. Zcash more than tripled in value this year, rising to $1,653 on Sept. 26 from $524 on Jan. 1, according to Token Terminal data. Its price more than doubled in the month following the ETF’s launch but has since fallen back to $770. The cryptocurrency remains up about 50% year to date.

Pandl described Zcash’s price appreciation over the past year as “Bitcoin’s Solana moment,” referring to Solana’s growing market cap and its challenge to Ethereum’s dominance as the “leading smart contract platform.”

“At 1.2% of Bitcoin’s market cap, I would still consider Zcash at a relatively low value,” he said, adding that Grayscale has no price targets for ZEC.

data.title: Pancontinental Energy Pursues Farmout Partner for Namibian PEL 87 Operation
data.description:
Pancontinental Energy is pressing ahead with its search for an offshore exploration partner in Namibia as early seismic reprocessing results point to an improvement in data quality across its flagship acreage.

The company told shareholders at its annual general meeting that attracting a suitably qualified and funded industry partner remained its overriding priority as it worked towards exploratory drilling in the Orange Basin.

Pancontinental operates petroleum exploration licence (PEL) 87 with a 75% working interest in the 10,970-square-kilometre permit, where it has identified eight prospects along the trend of the Venus and Mopane discoveries.

The portfolio carries a gross unrisked best estimate of 3.606 billion barrels in recoverable prospective oil resources, with 2.704 billion barrels attributable to Pancontinental’s interest.

The estimates relate to undiscovered accumulations and remain subject to both discovery and development risks.

Partner Search Remains Central

Pancontinental has taken the opportunity to major petroleum groups, large independent operators, and national oil companies, with discussions continuing despite the farmout process taking longer than management had initially anticipated.

“The board and management remain committed to securing a transaction that appropriately recognises the potential value of PEL 87 and introduces the financial and operational backing that is required to advance the project towards exploratory drilling,” chair Ernest Myers said in his AGM address.

“We recognise the importance of achieving a successful outcome and remain 100% focused on progressing discussions while further refining our technical understanding of the permit to reduce exploration uncertainty.”

The principal exploration targets lie within the Saturn Complex, which includes the Oryx and Hyrax prospects, and the Northern Channel.

Pancontinental is sharing results from its seismic pilot study with prospective partners as part of its efforts to address reservoir quality, the principal geological risk in the deepwater Orange Basin.

Seismic Work and Permit Renewal

Following a feasibility study and proposals from five contractors, Pancontinental awarded DUG Technology a contract to reprocess an initial 100km² of 3D seismic data.

The work aims to correct signal loss at target depths, with initial testing showing improved data quality and stronger seismic responses of the type observed at Venus and Mopane.

Pancontinental expects DUG to complete the pilot by mid-January 2027 and intends to begin reprocessing 4,200km² of 3D data covering its entire prospect inventory early next year.

The joint venture has proposed the larger seismic program alongside an existing firm commitment for one exploration well in its application to enter the second renewal exploration period.

The current exploration period expires on 22 January 2027, with the proposed two-year renewal awaiting ministerial approval following meetings with Namibian officials in Windhoek.

NZ Exploration Opportunity

Pancontinental is also pursuing an early-stage opportunity in New Zealand while maintaining expenditure discipline across its exploration portfolio.

The NZ Department of Petroleum and Minerals has accepted for evaluation the company’s application for a prospecting permit covering 9,972.5km² of the deepwater Taranaki Basin.

The proposed initial two-year work program would draw on existing 2D seismic data, with reprocessing, basin modelling, and prospect identification ahead of potential applications for exploration permits.

Pancontinental expects the application process to take approximately six months from the close of the competitive window on 8 October and plans to provide a detailed overview of the acreage’s potential if the permit is awarded.

data.title: Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates: Nifty bulls continue to push for 26,000; Crude prices rise
data.description:
Sensex Today | Stock Market LIVE Updates: Today is an important session for the Nifty bulls. The index is just about in the green for the week. It needs to close above 25,800 for a positive weekly close, which will be the fifth in a row.

The last instance of the Nifty gaining for five straight weeks was back in June and July of 2024, when it gained for eight weeks straight. One thing that the bulls may not like is the rebound in crude oil prices, as the Sub-$90 Brent crude is now nearing the mark of $97 to the barrel.

The Nifty has continued to find supply between the 25,950 and the 26,000 mark, as evident from the intraday highs of the last three sessions at 25,992, 25,951, and 25,973 respectively. The one positive from the week is that the index has made higher lows in the last four sessions, indicating that supports are shifting higher.

The Nifty Bank though, may snap a four-week losing streak in case it does not close above the 64,635 mark, which is exactly 1,100 points away from current levels. 64,000 - 64,150 levels continue to remain a supply zone, while 63,250 - 63,350 may act as a support.

Keep an eye on Tata Motors PV, NSE, International Gemmological Institute, and other stocks.

data.title: Fab-Form Industries Ltd. Announces Results for the Quarter Ended 30 September 2026
data.description:
Delta, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 26, 2026) - Fab-Form Industries Ltd. ("Fab-Form" or the "Company") announced today its financial results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, the first quarter of fiscal 2027. All amounts are in Canadian dollars unless otherwise stated.

Financial Highlights

Against the backdrop of a soft Canadian construction market and the Company's first quarter of direct operations in Missouri, the Company reports:

  • Revenue for the first quarter decreased 7.52% to $1,367,898 compared to $1,479,187 in the quarter ended 30 September 2025, mainly due to declines in Nudura Insulated Concrete Forms ("ICF") sales (-18.71%), the Company's largest product line, Helix (-85.83%), ICF accessories (-69.96%) and Monopour (-14.36%). The decrease was partially offset by growth in Bracing (+51.73%), Fast-Tube® (+94.07%) and Fastfoot® (+16.37%) sales. The growth in Bracing and Fastfoot® was mainly due to the establishment of the Company's Missouri operations.

  • Gross profit increased 2.11% to $533,349 from $522,333, and gross margin improved to 39.0% from 35.3%. Cost of sales fell 12.78%, faster than revenue, reflecting a shift in sales mix towards higher margin products, lower sales of low margin products and the contribution from Missouri.

  • Operating expenses increased 15.57% to $290,980. General and administrative expenses rose 28.77% to $233,319, mainly due to higher wages and benefits (+40.09%) and research and development expenses (+84.57%), while selling and marketing expenses fell 18.31% to $57,661.

  • Earnings from operations declined 10.42% to $242,369, compared to $270,553 in the same quarter last year. Operating margin was 17.7% compared to 18.3%.

  • Other income fell 95.20% to $2,246, compared to $46,840 in the same quarter last year, following the retirement of a short-term investment to acquire property in White Rock.

  • Net earnings for the quarter were $179,945 ($0.020 per share), down 24.21% from $237,434 ($0.026 per share) in the same quarter last year.

Financial Position

  • As of 30 September 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents of $1,788,621, up $193,280 (12.1%) from $1,595,341 at 30 June 2026 and up $451,912 (33.8%) from $1,336,709 at 30 September 2025.

  • Net cash generated from operating activities was $329,548 (2025: $362,982). Cash of $123,932 was used in investing activities, comprising property and equipment ($17,391), product development ($47,001) and intangible assets ($59,540). Cash of $30,566 was used in financing activities for lease payments on the Delta, BC office and warehouses.

  • Total assets grew to $7,844,954 from $7,436,824 at 30 June 2026, and shareholders' equity increased to $6,497,998 from $6,318,053.

  • The Company has no long-term debt other than lease liabilities, with total liabilities of $1,346,956, ensuring financial stability and flexibility for future growth.

Product and Market Update

Fab-Form continues to focus on its core product lines while advancing innovative solutions in concrete forming technology. Highlights for the quarter include:

U.S. Expansion - Missouri Branch

The Missouri branch generated revenue of $306,003 in its first quarter of operations, representing 22.4% of Company revenue. Its gross profit was $186,050, a gross margin of 60.8%, and it contributed 34.9% of Company gross profit. The decision to operate directly in Missouri responds to U.S. tariffs, the need for shorter delivery times for U.S. customers and a soft Canadian construction market. Tariffs are now paid only on steel costs rather than on selling prices, reducing the Company's exposure. Tariffs are expected to remain a challenge for steel exports to the U.S., and any further changes could affect steel product sales growth.

The Missouri location provides quick access to all U.S. states, supports distributors and contractors, and ties into the Company's target of US$3 million in additional revenue within 24 months. It also provides a base to introduce Fast-Tube® 3.0, Space-R™, Flex-R™, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle™ 2XK into the U.S. market.

Fast-Tube®

Fast-Tube® sales almost doubled, rising 94.07% to $82,224. In late September, a record test pour was completed at the Company's Springfield, Missouri warehouse, in which a 40-foot Fast-Tube® column was poured in just 70 minutes, a speed the Company believes no other forming system can match, and which demonstrates the pouring advantages Fast-Tube® offers contractors over cardboard tubes.

New Patent Applications and Zuckle™ 2XK

During the quarter the Company applied for two new patents, Ever-Wall™ and Zuckle 2XK™.

The Company also completed the design and specification of the new version of its drill adjustable wall aligner, Zuckle 2XK. Production of the first batch began shortly after quarter end, and the product is expected to be available to customers in mid-February 2027 from both the Delta, BC and Missouri locations. Recent test profiles show a load capacity approaching 13,000 lb, and the product has been engineered for low-cost production.

Forward-Looking Statements

Certain statements in this release constitute forward-looking information within the meaning of applicable securities laws. Such statements involve known and unknown risks, uncertainties, and other factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied by the forward-looking statements. Fab-Form Industries Ltd. does not undertake to update forward-looking statements, except as required by applicable laws.

About Fab-Form

Fab-Form Industries Ltd. is a leading innovator in concrete forming solutions, committed to enhancing construction efficiency and sustainability worldwide. The Company has been listed on the TSX Venture Exchange

data.title: Japan Tobacco up 2% on Imperial Brands takeover talk
data.description:
Shares in Japan Tobacco climbed 2% in early trading following a report it was considering partnering on a takeover of British cigarette maker Imperial Brands .

US tobacco group Altria said on Thursday it was considering a possible all-cash bid for Imperial Brands and was discussing a deal involving acquiring part of the British company's business with another party.

Tokyo-based JT is considering teaming up with a partner, Bloomberg News reported. JT declined to comment on the report.

Japan's benchmark index was up 1% in early trading.

The moves could set the stage for one of the largest deals in tobacco industry history and reflect pressure on cigarette makers to find new growth avenues as smoking rates fall.

Shares in Imperial, which said it had not received an approach but whose board would consider any proposal, jumped 13.8% on Thursday, giving it a £25.90 billion ($33.93 billion) market valuation.

Imperial would give a buyer a portfolio of established cigarette brands including Davidoff, Gauloises and Kool, which are sold in more than 100 markets.

"This deal would make a lot of sense for both (Altria) and JT, in our view, while we believe the deal could be done without impacting the current credit ratings of either name," BTIG analyst Owen Bennett said in a note.

JT, whose brands include Camel and Benson & Hedges, could take Imperial Brands assets in the US, Africa and the Middle East, Bennett said.

JT, whose shareholders include the Japanese government, said last week it would record an $8.7 billion loss after losing control of its Russian subsidiaries.

data.title: Gold steady, heads for weekly gain as markets await Fed signals
data.description:
Gold prices held steady on Friday and were headed for a modest weekly gain, as investors awaited further policy signals from the US Federal Reserve after strong inflation data cemented expectations of an interest-rate hike next month.

FUNDAMENTALS

* Spot gold was little changed at $3,567.33 per ounce by 0012 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.8% to $3,565.20. Bullion has risen about 1% so far this week.

* US markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.

* Markets fully expect a rate hike at the Fed's December policy meeting and price in a 66% chance of a larger, 50-basis-point increase in January, according to CME's FedWatch tool. The central bank last raised rates in September.

* Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

* Continued equity-market weakness puts gold at risk of breaking below $3,400 per ounce, HSBC said on Thursday.

* China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in October rose 1.6% from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.

* Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said on Thursday that the central bank must respond swiftly to signs of an inflation overshoot, including by accelerating the pace of rate hikes, keeping alive prospects of a rate increase as soon as December.

* Among other metals, spot silver fell 4.3% to $41.51 per ounce, but was headed for a modest weekly rise.

* Platinum gained 0.6% to $1,292.47, while palladium dropped 0.5% to $868.53 per ounce. Both metals were on track for weekly declines.

data.title: Haleon invests in 'Future of Health Innovation Hub', supported by Singapore EDB to advance Preventive Care across Asia Pacific
data.description:
• The partnership with the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB) will harness R&D, AI and digital technologies to accelerate science-backed innovations for Centrum, Caltrate and Sensodyne, meeting Asia's diverse needs in healthy ageing, health inclusivity and condition awareness.
  • Haleon will invest over S$100 million (US$80 million) for research and innovation for APAC, through its own R&D as well as partnerships with leading universities and collaboration with HealthTech startups.

SINGAPORE, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Haleon, a leading global Consumer Health company, today announced the establishment of its Future of Health Innovation Hub in Singapore, supported by the Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB). Through this Hub, Haleon will accelerate innovation across its Oral Health and Wellness brands including Sensodyne, Centrum and Caltrate and develop new science-backed products and packaging tailored to Asian consumers' needs. To support the Hub's ambitions, Haleon is investing over S$100 million (US$80 million) in research and innovation across APAC, spanning its own R&D capabilities, partnerships with leading universities and collaboration with HealthTech startups. This forms part of Haleon's existing annual R&D investment across APAC, reflecting the company's continued commitment to science-led innovation in the region.

Asia Pacific's Diverse Health ChallengesBy 2050, 1 in 4 people in Asia Pacific is expected to be aged 60 or over, representing nearly 1.3 billion people[1] and resulting in higher elderly-care costs. At the same time, 60% of Southeast Asia's working-age population is under 30[2]. Many markets also face pressure from healthcare workforce shortages – with an average of 1 doctor or less for every 1,000 people[3] – alongside gaps in public health infrastructure and rising non-communicable diseases. The opportunity for Haleon is to address the diverse needs of consumers - helping ageing individuals maintain independence and younger people stay healthy and productive.

From Consumer Insights to Trusted InnovationsIn Singapore, 60% of consumers report experiencing bone and joint issues, yet only 10% seek treatment, and in China approximately 90% adults have inadequate calcium intake, with just 20% taking calcium supplements[4]. To support bone-health, Haleon has introduced Caltrate in customised formats such as liquids and capsules, catering to local preferences. Similarly in the Philippines, where 90% lack iron, and over 75% are calcium deficient[5], Haleon has innovated Centrum packaging in single units, making key nutrients affordable and more accessible. For those seeking personalised health solutions like Korea and China, Haleon has introduced Centrum Daily Wellness Kits which provide nutrition tailored to specific life stages, such as menopause support for women over 50 and metabolic support for middle-aged adults.

Leveraging Singapore's Research and Innovation EcosystemTo further build on this series of innovation, Haleon's Future of Health Innovation Hub will combine deep consumer insights, scientific expertise, digital capabilities and AI-enabled technologies to accelerate the development of science-backed innovations further tailored to Asian consumers. Through partnerships with Singapore based academic institutions and government agencies and startups such as NUS Academy for Healthy Longevity (AHL), NTU Singapore Centre for Environmental Life Sciences Engineering (SCELSE), A*STAR's Institute of Human Development and Potential (IHDP), A*STAR's Institute of Molecular and Cell Biology (IMCB), the Asian Microbiome Library (AMILI) and Gray Matter Solutions (GMS), Haleon will invest in clinical studies, academic research and generate evidence to develop Asia-relevant innovations focused on healthy ageing, health inclusivity and condition awareness.

Dr. Keith Choy, President, Asia Pacific, Haleon, said: "Asia's diversity is its biggest opportunity. By understanding local needs from ageing populations to younger health-conscious consumers, our talented team is turning insights into science-backed innovations for our trusted brands such as Centrum, Caltrate and Sensodyne. Our partnership with the EDB will combine Singapore's research and innovation ecosystem with Haleon's trusted science and digital capabilities to advance preventive care and deliver better everyday health with humanity."

Turning Condition Awareness into Action with TechnologyHaleon aims to shift healthcare from treatment to prevention by helping people understand health conditions and seek proactive care. To help close this condition to treatment gap, Haleon will harness data and AI to understand health behaviours across Asia and inform future R&D and product innovation. Digital and AI-powered tools, including Caltrate Bone Density tool, Centrum Cognitive test and Sensodyne Tooth Sensitivity and Dental Ageing tools, will also be deployed across retail outlets, and Central Singapore Community Development Council events to build health literacy among consumers and expand access to Haleon's science-backed brands.

Ms. Ho Weng Si, Executive Vice President, Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), said: "Haleon's decision to anchor its Future of Health Innovation Hub in Singapore reflects the strength of our innovation ecosystem and the opportunities to advance Consumer Health solutions from Singapore for Asia Pacific. By bringing together industry, academia, healthcare and technology partners, this collaboration will accelerate clinical research and consumer insights into science-backed innovations that support healthier ageing and better health outcomes across the region. We look forward to deepening our partnership with Haleon as it builds new innovation capabilities and creates opportunities for the Singapore workforce to shape the future of Consumer Health."

  • [1] Source: https://asiapacific.unfpa.org/en/topics/ageing

  • [2] Source: https://amata.com/news-media/362-southeast-asia-s-young-workforce-a-big-plus-for-investors

  • [3] Source: Bain & Company, Asia-Pacific Front Line of Healthcare 2026 (health worker density data)

  • [4] Source: Haleon consolidation of third-party market data including IQVIA, Circana, NIQ

  • [5] Source: Angeles-Agdeppa, Imelda et al. "Food sources, energy and nutrient intakes of adults: 2013 Philippines National Nutrition Survey." Nutrition journal vol. 18,1 59. 10 Oct. 2019, doi:10.1186/s12937-019-0481-z

About Haleon

Haleon (LSE/) is a consumer company that is solely focused on better everyday health. Our people, our brands, our research, our investment and our innovation are aimed at improving the everyday health of consumers. Our product portfolio spans six major categories - Oral Health, Vitamins, Minerals and Supplements (VMS), Pain Relief, Respiratory Health, Digestive Health and Therapeutic Skin Health and Other. Our superior brands - such as Advil, Centrum, Otrivin, Panadol, parodontax, Polident, Sensodyne, Theraflu and Voltaren – are trusted by more than one billion consumers and are recommended by health professionals around the world.

For more information, please visit www.haleon.com

data.title: South Korea's November Exports Likely Accelerated on Brisk Chip Demand — Market Talk
data.description: South Korea's exports likely accelerated in November on brisk chip demand, Citigroup' Jin-Wook Kim says. The global artificial-intelligence boom continues to drive strong semiconductor shipments overseas with the country's trade surplus widening, the economist writes in a note. Citi expects South Korea's exports to have climbed 105.4% from a year earlier, faster than revised 93.9% growth in October. Citi expects the country's trade surplus to widen to $53.6 billion from revised $42.6 billion in the previous month. For the first 20 days of November, the country's chip exports nearly quadrupled from a year earlier, keeping them on course for another monthly record. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)

data.title: Update on Reverse Takeover Transaction
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    VANCOUVER, British Columbia – TheNewswire – November 26, 2026 - Madoro Metals Corp. (“Madoro” or the “Company”) (TSX VENTURE: MDM; OTC: MSTXF; FSE: A2QQ1X), is pleased to provide a further update regarding the proposed reverse takeover transaction with Narrow River Resources Pty Ltd. (“NRR”) previously announced in the Company’s news release dated February 2, 2026, and as most recently updated in the Company’s news release dated September 29, 2026 (the “Proposed Transaction”).

    Madoro and NRR continue to advance the remaining components required under TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”) Policy 5.2 – Changes of Business and Reverse Takeovers in connection with the Proposed Transaction. The Company has received comments from the TSXV in connection with its review of the Proposed Transaction. Madoro and NRR, together with their respective advisors, are actively working through those comments and completing the remaining transaction documentation and disclosure materials required to advance the Proposed Transaction.

    Subject to completion of the TSXV’s review and receipt of the required TSXV approval, the Company currently anticipates holding the shareholder meeting required to approve the Proposed Transaction during the first quarter of 2027. The meeting date has not yet been fixed and will be announced once the TSXV authorizes Madoro to hold a special meeting in connection with the Proposed Transaction.

    Accordingly, the Company has elected to hold its annual meeting of shareholders on December 15, 2026. Shareholders are encouraged to consult the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca for further details.

    As previously announced, the Company has entered into a definitive share purchase agreement with 9525-9867 Québec Inc. and NRR in respect of the Proposed Transaction. The parties remain committed to advancing the Proposed Transaction and will provide further updates as appropriate.

    Considering the revised timing for the Proposed Transaction, the Company and NRR have revised the size and composition of the previously announced concurrent non-brokered private placement (the “Private Placement”), having regard to the anticipated financing requirements of the resulting issuer. The revised terms of the Private Placement are for aggregate gross proceeds of up to C$1,450,000, comprised entirely of hard dollar units (“HD Units”). Under the Private Placement, the Company proposes to issue 29,000,000 HD Units at a price of C$0.05 per HD Unit. There will no longer be any flow-through units offered as part of the Private Placement. Each HD Unit will consist of one common share of the Company (a “Common Share”) and one-half of one common share purchase warrant (each whole warrant, an “HD Warrant”).  Each HD Warrant will entitle the holder to purchase one Common Share at a price of C$0.08 for a period of two (2) years from the Closing. Completion of the Private Placement in connection with the Proposed Transaction will remain subject to TSXV acceptance and all other required regulatory approvals.

    Completion of the Proposed Transaction remains subject to, among other things, regulatory and shareholder approvals, TSXV acceptance, completion of the Private Placement, finalization and mailing of the Circular, completion of ancillary transaction documentation, and satisfaction of other customary closing conditions.

As a result of this third amendment, and following completion of the Final Payment, the Company shall have completed the Option, thereby acquiring a 100% interest in the First Green Lithium Property. The Amendment Agreement remains subject to the approval of the TSXV.

data.title: Laserbond Forecasts First-Half Shortfall After Weak Start to FY27
data.description:
Laserbond Limited expects revenue of between $19 million and $20m for the six months to 31 December 2026 after a recovery in second-quarter trading failed to compensate for a weak start to the financial year.

The specialist surface engineering company anticipates first-half revenue and earnings will fall below the corresponding period of the previous financial year despite activity returning to normal levels in the second quarter.

Laserbond expects a materially stronger second half in line with the corresponding period of the previous financial year, with forward orders already tracking ahead of expectations.

The recovery is being supported by improving customer demand, an expanding customer base and the early commercialisation of a new hard chrome replacement coating.

Cash holdings increased from $2.9m at 30 June to $4.8m at 31 October.

Products and Services Soft

Trading across the Products and Services businesses has remained softer than Laserbond anticipated at its October annual general meeting, despite an improvement in sales orders since the first quarter.

A major original equipment manufacturer (OEM) customer in the Products business continues to draw down stocks accumulated in 2025 in anticipation of tungsten carbide shortages and rising prices, although orders have stabilised and lifted in recent weeks.

The Services business has encountered weaker demand from mining customers—particularly on the east coast, where sustained high diesel prices have prompted operators to defer scheduled servicing and cut maintenance expenditure.

Laserbond expects its 40% interest in the strongly performing Perth-based Gateway business to provide a partial earnings offset to the weaker trading conditions elsewhere.

New Coating Opportunity

Laserbond has delivered its first commercial sale using a new coating process that brings the cost of laser cladding close to that of conventional hard chrome plating, estimating the hard chrome replacement opportunity could increase its addressable market by 10 to 12 times.

The company is pursuing additional sales in the adjacent market ahead of the formal product launch scheduled for the third quarter of the 2027 financial year.

Its new Yatala facility in Queensland remains on track to begin production in the fourth quarter, doubling capacity and providing anticipated efficiency and network utilisation benefits from the 2028 financial year.

The actions we are taking, including streamlining our production network to grow capacity closer to our customers, are part of a deliberate strategy to strengthen the core of the business now, scale proven solutions into new markets and geographies over the medium term, and position Laserbond as a globally relevant technology and solutions leader over the longer term,” chief executive officer Rob Freeman said.

“We are confident this process will deliver a much stronger second half and a better business well beyond it.”

Broadening Major Customers

Laserbond has reduced its exposure to the two major OEM customers that have contributed most to volatility in its financial results in recent years.

The addition of Komatsu and Metal7 has doubled the number of OEM customers to four, with a fifth partnership expected in the third quarter.

Komatsu’s first laser cladding cell is operational following delivery on time and on budget, while Laserbond expects further domestic and international licensing contracts during the current financial year.

The Metal7 collaboration provides a route into the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, North Africa, and India, with Laserbond anticipating Metal7 will become a major OEM customer within one to two years.

Excluding Komatsu, Laserbond expects most revenue from its new OEM relationships to flow from FY28 onward.

data.title: China Shenhua Energy Plans $860 Million Fund Raise to Pare Debt
data.description:
By P.R. Venkat

China Shenhua Energy plans to raise about 6.74 billion Hong Kong dollars, equivalent to US$860 million, through a share placement to pare debt.

The coal and power company will place 177.0 million new H shares at HK$38.10 each, it said in a filing on Friday.

The placement price represents a 7.70% discount to Thursday's closing price of HK$41.28.

About 90% of the proceeds will be used to repay onshore debt, which rose after a large acquisition earlier this year, the company said.

Borrowings reached 157.63 billion yuan at the end of June, following a 93.52 billion yuan cash payment to acquire stakes in 12 companies from its state-owned parent, China Energy Investment.

The remaining proceeds will be allocated to working capital, primarily for tax payments. The transaction is expected to close Dec. 1.

China International Capital Corp. and CLSA are acting as placing agents.

data.title: CORPWATCH: India clears SBI Mutual Fund for near-10% South Indian Bank stake
data.description:
India's central bank has cleared SBI Mutual Fund to own up to 9.99% of South Indian Bank, a Kerala lender with no controlling shareholder, the bank said on November 23.

Thrissur-based South Indian Bank heard from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) that day and told the exchanges that evening. The clearance is subject to banking, foreign-exchange and securities rules. One scheme of the fund, which is managed by State Bank of India's listed asset manager SBI Funds Management , held 2.9% at the end of September, according to the bank's shareholding pattern.

SBI Mutual Fund is the second large Indian financial group allowed to build a near-10% position in the bank this year, after the group of Kotak Mahindra Bank was cleared on May 6. A Kotak Multicap Fund scheme was the largest single holder on September 30 with 6.05%, ahead of Bandhan Small Cap Fund on 4.69% and non-resident investor Yusuffali M.A. on 4.30%, while small retail investors owned 37%. Two blocks of almost 10% each would leave a pair of domestic fund groups with the loudest voices in a bank where nobody else holds even 5%.

South Indian Bank shareholders above 1% at September 30, 2026. Source: South Indian Bank shareholding pattern filed with the National Stock Exchange of India. IntelliNews

Filings by target banks to the National Stock Exchange show at least 16 RBI approvals in 2026 for groups to hold just under 10% of nine mid-tier private lenders.

RBI rules require prior approval for any holding of 5% or more. RBL Bank's filing on SBI Mutual Fund shows the conditions: a year to buy, a hard ceiling of 9.99% and fresh approval needed to climb back above 5% if the stake slips below it. An early case under the new rules came in December 2025, when the RBI let HDFC Bank group entities hold up to 9.5% of IndusInd Bank , with HDFC Bank saying it had no plan to invest directly.

RBI approvals in 2026 for investor groups to hold up to 9.95-9.99% of mid-tier Indian private lenders. Source: Regulation 30 filings by each bank to the National Stock Exchange of India. IntelliNews

Foreign buyers have gone further. Dubai's Emirates NBD was allotted 60% of RBL Bank on June 18 for INR260.16bn ($2.8bn), and its Indian branches fold into RBL on December 1. Its voting rights are still capped at 26% under the Banking Regulation Act, the RBI's April approval states, so minority blocks still count at RBL. Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, which agreed in May 2025 to buy 20% of Yes Bank , held 24.9% at the end of September.

In October the government picked a Canadian unit of Fairfax Financial Holdings to buy 60.72% of IDBI Bank for INR528.78bn, which the finance ministry calls the biggest foreign direct investment in India's financial sector. Fairfax still has to pass the RBI's fit-and-proper review.

None of the fund-house filings signals a bid, and a 9.99% block is a long way from a merger vote. Yet three Mumbai-based financial groups are now cleared for big minority stakes across nine mid-tier banks, while foreign investors take large or controlling stakes in others, including two former problem lenders, Yes Bank and IDBI Bank.

South Indian Bank's net profit rose 21% y/y to INR4.26bn in the July-September quarter, according to its results, and its gross non-performing loan ratio fell to 1.24% from 2.93%. The shares closed at INR58.87 on November 23, valuing the bank at about INR154bn.

data.title: Nikkei Rises 0.4%, Led by Banks, Trading Houses — Market Talk
data.description:
1915 ET - Japanese stocks are higher in early trade as recent selloffs in artificial intelligence-related stocks ease. Banks and trading houses are leading the gains. Mizuho Financial Group is up 3.5% and Marubeni is 3.4% higher. The dollar is at 159.34 yen, compared with Y159.17 as of Thursday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are focusing on energy prices and their implications for central bank policymaking. The Nikkei Stock Average is up 0.4% at 57754.22. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)

1846 ET - Japanese stocks may remain rangebound as uncertainty continues over the pace of data-center buildout and profitability of artificial-intelligence businesses. Nikkei futures are up 0.7% at 57810 on the SGX. The dollar is at 159.26 yen, compared with Y159.17 as of Thursday's Tokyo stock market close. Investors are focusing on energy prices and their implications for central bank policymaking. The Nikkei Stock Average rose 0.9% to 57499.16 on Thursday. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com)

1117 ET - The U.S. Federal Reserve could increase interest rates by as much as 100 basis points over the coming year even with a slowdown in the artificial-intelligence industry, Macro Hive's Dominique Dwor-Frecaut says in a note. "I do not expect an AI bust to trigger [a recession] or to bring inflation sustainably back to target on its own," she says. The Fed needs to raise rates to bring inflation close to its 2% target, Dwor-Frecaut says. Markets price in two rate increases by the Fed by March 2027 and a 76% chance of a third rate rise by June, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

1005 ET - The euro stays modestly higher against the dollar after news that European governments picked Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to be the next president of the European Central Bank. The news didn't come as a surprise as he was considered a front-runner for the role. In 2024, Hernandez de Cos joked that he was an "owl" when asked whether he was a "hawk" or "dove," emphasizing his focus on data rather than leaning in favor of tightening or loosening policy. The euro rises 0.1% to $1.0977--little changed from levels before the announcement. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0945 ET - Safe-haven demand has provided some support to the Japanese yen this month even as the dollar strengthens, MUFG Bank's Lee Hardman says in a note. The yen has remained stable against the dollar while rising against nondollar currencies. "The heightened threat of further intervention from Japan to support the yen if dollar-yen rises beyond the 160.00 level is also helping to provide support." Moreover, the Bank of Japan is expected to deliver faster rate hikes including another quarter-point rate rise in December. However, the BOJ's normalization of policy hasn't been sufficient yet to trigger a significant reversal lower for the dollar versus the yen, he says. The dollar trades flat at 159.17 yen. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0944 ET - Minutes from the European Central Bank's October meeting confirm that an interest-rate hike in December appears likely, Carsten Brzeski at ING says in a note. While the central bank voted to keep rates unchanged, several members openly advocated for a hike. This sends a clear signal that a rate increase on Dec. 18 is a done deal if inflation concerns remain elevated, Brzeski says. While oil prices have fallen since October, they aren't much lower than when September's staff projections were conducted, he notes. But the path is less clear beyond December. Much will depend on the pass-through of energy prices to other areas of the economy, Brzeski says, adding that additional hikes in 2027 could do more harm than good. (don.forbes@wsj.com)

0920 ET - The U.S. dollar's correlation to equities is unreliable, HSBC foreign exchange strategists say in a note. The dollar is caught between its role as a safe haven and the implications of stock market moves, particularly in AI stocks, on U.S. growth, they say. HSBC is cautiously positive on the dollar's outlook, expecting the Federal Reserve to remain hawkish and the U.S. economy to stay resilient. The bank is also upbeat on U.S. equities on the AI theme. "Our caution centers on the fickle equity relationship," the strategists say. The risk is that renewed stock weakness could dampen U.S. rate-rise expectations with no guarantee that safe-haven demand for the dollar would compensate, they say. The DXY dollar index trades flat at 103.654. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

0900 ET - Unstable geopolitics and persistent inflation will weigh on growth in capital markets activity next year, Deutsche Bank analysts write in a report. "The outlook for 2027 is broadly constructive, but risks remain high," says Christian Nolting, the bank's chief investment strategist. Geopolitical tensions won't cool, while high energy prices and trade barriers will result in higher-for-longer inflation, the report's authors say. Interest rates will therefore likely stay stubbornly high, they say. Artificial-intelligence investment will continue, with infrastructure companies a particular beneficiary, but the pace of the AI boom will slow, the strategists say. "AI alone is not enough," Nolting says. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)

0838 ET - The Bank of England is unlikely to increase interest rates three more times as priced in by markets, PIMCO's Rupert Harrison says in a note. The most recent U.K. inflation data show no evidence of higher energy prices spilling into core goods and service prices, lowering the need for the BOE to raise rates aggressively, he says. The BOE could raise rates two more times over the coming months, if the U.K. inflation data momentum continues, Harrison says. Markets price in a 90% chance of a BOE rate increase in December, and two more rate rises by July 2027, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

0803 ET - Ahead of the Spanish general election on Sunday, political parties are offering different approaches to boost household income, Pablo Muylle at ING says in a note. The governing Socialist Party wants to continue raising statutory wages while cutting working hours and expanding social support. The main opposition Partido Popular is focused instead on tax relief and stable-employment incentives, while the far-right Vox has proposed broader tax cuts, deregulation and welfare cuts. All proposals carry risks, with higher wage floors and shorter hours potentially hitting low-productivity employers, while tax cuts tend to miss the lowest earners, Muylle says. "The challenge for the next government will be to raise disposable incomes without weakening employment or creating unsustainable fiscal commitments." (don.forbes@wsj.com)

0738 ET - The mere stabilization of oil prices at current levels is not enough for the central banks of developed economies to keep interest rates unchanged, Muzinich & Co's Erick Muller says in a note. "Oil prices will likely continue to feature prominently among the factors monitored by the bond market," he says. A "neither war nor peace" situation is hardly sustainable, says Muller, adding that it would keep a high risk premium embedded in crude oil prices. "The longer oil prices remain elevated, the greater the risk that they will significantly feed through into core inflation," he says. Muzinich expects both the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank to raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

0733 ET - Scope Ratings expects credit rating gaps between Europe's traditional core and periphery to continue to narrow, it says in its sovereign outlook for 2027. Greece, Cyprus, Portugal and Spain, all with recent positive rating actions, are expected to reduce debt significantly by 2031, Scope says. "Conversely, we continue to see pressures for France, Poland, Belgium and Austria, countries which are running expansionary fiscal policy despite high and rising debt levels," it says. Among Central and Eastern European countries, rating trends for Poland and Hungary are likely to converge, it says. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Japan Tobacco shares up 1% after Imperial Brands report
data.description:
Shares in Japan Tobacco (JT) climbed 1%, in line with the benchmark index , following a report it was considering a deal for British cigarette maker Imperial Brands .

US tobacco group Altria said on Thursday it was considering a possible all-cash bid for Imperial Brands and was discussing a deal involving part of the British company's business with another party.

Tokyo-based JT is considering teaming up with a partner, Bloomberg News reported. JT declined to comment on the report.
